newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise, peso issues lead the way.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise, peso issues lead the way.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late Monday with peso-denominated issues leading the way, testifying to the strong underlying tone in the market.

"Peso bonds had a good day. The market is firm but a bit tired," said a trader at an Argentine bank, referring to the fact that the market is bumping up against resistance levels after the recent gains.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 87-1/2, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.10 to 124.30.
The peso-denominated Bocon Proveedor due 2007 rose 0.25 pesos to 96.95.
"The market is very well bid in a tight range. It is testing resistance levels," said an analyst at a foreign bank. He said the FRB is struggling to break the 87-5/8 to 88 level.
Traders were looking to the release of U.S. consumer prices and Argentina's auction of 250 million pesos of 91-, and 250 million pesos of 182-day Letes Tuesday.
Traders expected the auction to go well, considering the current high levels of liquidity.
Call money rates fell to 5.53 percent from 5.65 percent.
